newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 3.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- U.S. spy satellite detects long-range cruise missiles being developed by South Korea: The missile development contravenes U.S.-Korea missile agreement: Washington Times quoting American intelligence officials.
- 11 international drug trafficking rings uncovered, 38 drug runners arrested in Korea.
- National Assembly fails to act on '97 budget by December 2 deadline as government and opposition camps failed to iron out differing positions on pending issues.
- Bankruptcies in manufacturing sector soar up, reaching 507 cases in October, accounting for 44 percent of total bankruptcies.
- Government to remove statutory severance pay system after 2000: workers currently covered by the severance system are kept intact: Prime Minister Lee to issue statement on the matter today.
- President Kim in a meeting with government party functionaries yesterday, renews his earlier stance to press for North Korea's apology for September submarine incursion incident.
- U.S., North Korea end talks on liaison offices: Japan's Mainichi Shimbun: South Korea's Foreign Ministry dismissed Mainich story as 'totally groundless.'
